content: How to Log In It is not mandatory to log in to view or edit pages. However, logging in provides additional features and is generally recommended. Logging In To create a user account, you must provide a username (this can be your real name or a nickname) and a password. If the username you choose is already in use, the system will reject it. Once your account is created, you are considered logged in. For subsequent logins, you will need to enter your username and verify your identity by providing the correct password. Any edits you make while logged in will be attributed to your username. If you are not logged in, your edits will be recorded under your IP address. Some MediaWiki projects operate as a family, meaning that logging in applies to the entire family of projects, and shared preference settings are used. This is particularly true for the over 1,000 Wikia projects. However, on Wikimedia projects, logging in and setting preferences must currently be done separately for each wiki. For more information, refer to the Single Login feature. If you are not logged in, you can view your IP address by checking the page history. Why Log In? You are not required to log in to read or edit any MediaWiki wiki. Most pages can be edited by anyone, even without logging in. However, there are several advantages to logging in: 1. Recognition by Other Users: When you make changes to pages, other users can identify you by your username. Using an IP address as an identifier is less practical, especially if you use different devices or locations (e.g., home, office, or public spaces). Even at the same location, your IP address may vary depending on the internet connection. A username provides a consistent identity. 2. Personal User Page and Talk Page: Logging in allows you to create a user page where you can share information about yourself and a user talk page for communication with other users. 3. Marking Edits as Minor: You can mark edits as minor, which helps other users distinguish between significant and minor changes. 4. Tracking Changes: You can monitor changes to pages of interest using a watchlist. 5. Email Communication: If you provide an email address, other users can contact you via email without knowing your actual email address. This feature is optional, and you are not required to provide an email address if you prefer not to. 6. Renaming Pages: Logged-in users can rename pages. 7. Customizing Preferences: You can set your own preferences, such as the number of pages displayed in Recent Changes or the appearance of the site (e.g., fonts, colors, and layout) by selecting different skins. How to Log In Before logging in, ensure that your browser accepts cookies. Click the Log in link at the top right of the page. You will be prompted to enter your username and password. If you are logging in for the first time, use the provided link to create an account. You may optionally provide an email address, which allows other users to contact you anonymously. If you select the Remember me option, you will not need to re-enter your password when accessing the wiki from the same computer. Note that this feature will not work if your password was generated by the MediaWiki software. In such cases, you should change your password. Logging in and setting preferences must be done separately for each wiki. To maintain a consistent identity across multiple wikis, consider using the same username on each wiki, provided the name is available. Troubleshooting Login Issues Case Sensitivity Usernames and passwords are case-sensitive. Ensure that you enter the correct capitalization. For example, if your username is MyUserName, you cannot log in as myusername. The only exception is the first character of the username, which is capitalized by default. Registration on the Correct Wiki If you registered on a different version of the wiki, you will need to create a new username for the current version. Enabling Cookies If you appear to log in successfully but are logged out immediately after viewing a page, this is likely a cookie issue. Ensure that cookies are enabled in your browser. Also, check that your computer's date and time are set correctly, as incorrect settings can cause cookies to expire prematurely. Some firewall or ad-blocking software may interfere with the cookies used to maintain your login session. Immediate Logout Some internet service providers (ISPs) use transparent proxies that can cause login issues. If you are automatically logged out after logging in, and clearing your cookies does not resolve the problem, try using the secure server to bypass the proxy. This issue is more common with certain satellite ISPs, such as HughesNet or DirecWay. Occasional Logouts You may occasionally find yourself logged out between starting and saving an edit or when switching between multiple wiki pages in different browser windows. This can result from browser cookie, cache, or firewall settings. Additionally, due to the nature of the MediaWiki software, some user ID information is stored on the servers. During periods of heavy server load, the system may experience glitches, causing your ID information to be misplaced and resulting in a logout. Best Solution To avoid being logged out unexpectedly, select the Remember me option when logging in. If you are using a public or shared computer, ensure that you erase your user ID cookies after your session or click the Log out button. What If I Forget My Password? If you provided an email address during account creation or in your preferences, you can retrieve your account by entering your username on the login screen and selecting Email new password. A temporary password will be sent to your email address. If you did not provide an email address or if the address is outdated, you will need to create a new account. Creating an Account To create an account, click Log in at the top right of the page and then select Create an account. You will need to provide a username, password, and complete a CAPTCHA (a visual test to distinguish humans from automated systems). If you cannot view CAPTCHAs, you can request an account to be created for you. Since September 26, 2006, usernames cannot include the @ symbol. Setting Preferences Click the Preferences link at the top right of the page to access various options, including changing your password and selecting a different skin to alter the appearance of the site. For more details, refer to the Help:Preferences page. User Page and User Talk Page As a logged-in user, you can create your own user page and user talk page. Your username will be displayed at the top right of the page. Clicking on it will take you to your user page, which you can edit like any other wiki page. Most users write a brief introduction about themselves and their interests on their user page. You also have a user talk page, accessible by clicking the Talk link next to your username. Other users can leave messages on your talk page, and you can respond to them. How to Log Out You can log out at any time by clicking the Log out link at the top right of the page. If your username contains characters that are easily confused (e.g., lowercase l and uppercase I), consider registering a secondary account with a clearer username to prevent impersonation. However, since the implementation of stricter account creation rules, accounts similar to existing ones can only be created by administrators.
